Physical_Relationship: MV201 valve state <-> FIT201 flow physical consistency
Engineering_Rationale: A motorized valve's commanded position should be physically consistent with the flow sensor immediately downstream: CLOSED implies ~zero flow, OPEN implies steady flow; a mismatch would indicate a stuck valve, spoofed sensor, or manipulated actuator.
Coverage: VALIDATION NORMAL=99.578%, ATTACK=100.000% (event-based); continuous feature coverage=99.58%
Robustness: S2_R1_score means: TRAIN-NORMAL=0.6172, TRAIN-ATTACK=0.8931, VALIDATION-NORMAL=0.5679, VALIDATION-ATTACK=0.9918 -- a modest TRAIN-NORMAL to VALIDATION-NORMAL shift exists (0.617 -> 0.568) but a much larger, consistent NORMAL-to-ATTACK gap is preserved in both splits.
Main_Limitation: Requires detecting the full 3-state sequence, not a simple 2-state transition; only 64 usable NORMAL TRAIN sequences; transitional-state dwell time varies (median 7.0s), so the true 'moment of opening' has some inherent jitter; VALIDATION attack-period coverage for this exact sequence has not yet been confirmed nonzero (see Part 4).
Decision_Rationale: Physical relationship well-supported (n=64, consistency=100.0%), AND a continuously-evaluable feature exists with 99.6% VALIDATION coverage that is NOT saturated (VALIDATION-NORMAL mean=0.568 < 0.9).

Physical_Relationship: P205 (bleach/NaOCl dosing pump) activation -> AIT203 (ORP) response
Engineering_Rationale: Activating the hypochlorite dosing pump should raise oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) within a characteristic delay -- a standard dosing-pump/analyzer engineering relationship.
Coverage: VALIDATION NORMAL=0.180%, ATTACK=0.000% (event-based); continuous feature coverage=100.00%
Robustness: Event-based S2_R2_score coverage is too sparse to assess NORMAL-vs-ATTACK drift directly in VALIDATION (0 ATTACK samples evaluable). The state-conditioned fallback (S2_R2_state_fallback_score) shows VALIDATION-NORMAL mean=0.9783 vs VALIDATION-ATTACK mean=0.9930 -- both are SATURATED near the ceiling (1.0), consistent with the known TRAIN-to-VALIDATION AIT-series distribution shift documented in the RF diagnostic (script 04); the two classes are not practically distinguishable via this fallback.
Main_Limitation: n=64 usable TRAIN NORMAL events; response magnitude is large and clear; no VALIDATION-ATTACK transitions of this actuator were found in the prior transition-only analysis, so attack behavior for this exact rule remains untested under the transition-triggered formulation.
Decision_Rationale: Physical relationship well-supported (n=64, consistency=98.4%), BUT practical use is constrained: the available fallback feature is saturated in VALIDATION (NORMAL mean=0.978 >= 0.9, barely distinguishable from ATTACK mean=0.993).

Physical_Relationship: P205 (bleach pump) <-> P203 (acid pump) bidirectional transition coupling
Engineering_Rationale: The two dosing pumps are expected to switch together (both ON or both OFF) as part of the same pH/ORP control loop; a mismatch would indicate one pump is not responding to the shared control signal.
Coverage: VALIDATION NORMAL=0.180%, ATTACK=0.000% (event-based); continuous feature coverage=100.00%
Robustness: S2_R3B_state_mismatch means: TRAIN-NORMAL=0.000094, TRAIN-ATTACK=0.003735 (~40x higher under attack), VALIDATION-NORMAL=0.000000, VALIDATION-ATTACK=0.000000 -- both remain near the floor (0), i.e. NOT saturated, unlike S2-R2's fallback.
Main_Limitation: The event-based coupling_consistent companion feature remains sparse (0.059% VALIDATION coverage); TRAIN-NORMAL mismatch rate, while low, is not exactly zero (0.0094%), so the steady-state equality assumption is a very strong but not perfectly absolute regularity.
Decision_Rationale: Physical relationship well-supported (n=59, consistency=100.0%), AND a continuously-evaluable feature exists with 100.0% VALIDATION coverage that is NOT saturated (VALIDATION-NORMAL mean=0.000 < 0.9).

Physical_Relationship: P203 (acid/HCl dosing pump) activation -> AIT202 (pH) response
Engineering_Rationale: Activating the acid dosing pump should lower pH within a characteristic delay -- the mirror-image dosing-pump/analyzer relationship to S2-R2.
Coverage: VALIDATION NORMAL=0.180%, ATTACK=0.000% (event-based); continuous feature coverage=0.03%
Robustness: Not assessable via a fallback: the steady-state separation check in script 09 found AIT202's OFF/ON distributions by P203 state were NOT cleanly separated enough (SMD=-1.066 but IQR overlap fraction=0.282, exceeding the documented <0.25 bar) to build a defensible fallback at all -- no fallback exists for this rule.
Main_Limitation: n=64 usable TRAIN NORMAL events; response magnitude is small, closer to the sensor noise floor; no VALIDATION-ATTACK transitions of this actuator were found in the prior transition-only analysis, so attack behavior for this exact rule remains untested under the transition-triggered formulation.
Decision_Rationale: Physical relationship well-supported (n=64, consistency=95.3%), BUT practical use is constrained: no continuously-evaluable feature reaches 90% VALIDATION coverage (best=0.029%).
